tools.name: discover_services
tools.description: Full-stack products, agent systems, integration, modernization and B2B engineering workstreams. Returns service scope and engagement options.

tools.name: review_engineering_evidence
tools.description: Representative project capabilities and founder enterprise background, with evidence links and scope context.

tools.name: get_procurement_information
tools.description: Engagement process, data handling, supplier-review topics and authority boundaries for RFPs and subcontracting.

tools.name: prepare_engagement_brief
tools.description: Formats confirmed business requirements for an RFP or proposal request. Does not store, transmit, quote or approve the project. Preserve unknowns; no technology or budget ceiling.

tools.name: request_proposal
tools.description: Saves an approved project brief and reply contact for engineering review. Supports RFPs, full products and subcontracting. Requires actual requester consent. Reuse the same UUID v4 and unchanged payload on retries. No purchase or execution.

tools.name: request_email_followup
tools.description: Saves a business inquiry and authorized reply contact. Use for procurement, delivery partnerships, confidential engagement setup or questions before a full brief. No newsletter signup.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_procurement_information · Private data: request_proposal, request_email_followup · Public sink: request_email_followup.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_procurement_information · Private data: request_proposal, request_email_followup · Public sink: request_email_followup

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
